title: docs(layout): each page snippet names the `pageType` that draws its heading, or puts it in a `page:header` block (objectui#11423)
body:
Fixes #11423

Clause-②: no

## What changed

`content/docs/guide/layout.md` had four page snippets that set `title` (one also set `description`) and named no `pageType`. A page with no `pageType` is a `record` page. `PageRenderer` leaves a record page's `h1` to a `page:header` block and never draws its `description`, so each copied snippet drew no heading. Each passage now names the page type it teaches:

| Passage | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Page Component › Basic Usage | `"pageType": "app"` | It teaches the page's own header on a general page whose body is a placeholder. `app` is the spec's "App-level page with navigation context", and the Page Header reference's "Usage in a Page" already uses `app` for a Users page. |
| With Action Buttons | `"pageType": "list"` | A products grid with buttons above it. That is the spec's `list` kind, "Record list/grid surface with switchable visualizations + quick actions". |
| Detail Page with Actions | `"pageType": "record"` named; the page-level `title` removed; the heading moved into a `page:header` block (`"properties": { "title": "Acme Corporation" }`) after the breadcrumb | A detail page is a record page, so its heading belongs to `page:header`. The buttons stay `action:button` nodes in `children`: header `actions` are action ids resolved against a bound object, and this snippet binds none. |
| Best Practices 3 | `"pageType": "list"` | A list of orders with a "New Order" button. The passage's own follow-up already contrasts it with a record page. |

Prose: Basic Usage gains a short paragraph on what `pageType` decides and what a page without one draws. The Detail passage says why its heading is a `page:header` block. With Action Buttons and Best Practices 3 each gain one clause. The Schema API block's comments on `title`, `description` and `pageType` now say that a `record` page draws neither key.

Every value taught is a member of the spec's `PageTypeSchema` (record, home, app, utility, list).

## Measured first

These are one-time render probes through the real `SchemaRenderer` and the real renderers. The probe file was not committed.

At BASE `a1a44d621`, each fence verbatim:
- Basic Usage renders as `data-page-type="record"` with no `h1`, and the description is not drawn. The only text is "User list goes here".
- With Action Buttons, Detail Page with Actions and Best Practices 3 render as `record` with no `h1`. Their buttons are drawn.
- With `pageType` set to app, list, utility or home, the Basic Usage document draws the `h1` "User Management" and the description. With `record` it draws neither.

On the corrected shapes:
- The Detail document, with `record` and the `page:header` block, draws exactly one `h1`, "Acme Corporation", inside the header block. Its only buttons are Edit and Delete.
- The same `page:header` with `title` written flat on the node is refused by both faces (`invalid_union` at `children`). That is why the snippet uses the `properties` bag shown in the guide's Page Header section.
- Both faces (`safeValidateSchema` and `StrictAnyComponentSchema`) accept all four corrected documents. `page-width-padding-refusal-11318.test.ts` already runs every page fence of the guide through both faces, unchanged and green.

## The pin

New file `packages/components/src/__tests__/guide-layout-page-headings-11423.test.tsx`. It derives every `type: "page"` JSON fence of the guide that authors a heading, either as the page's `title` or as a titled `page:header` block in its children. Each one is rendered through the real `SchemaRenderer` and must draw exactly one `h1` with that text. A heading drawn by a `page:header` block must sit inside that block; a heading the page draws itself must not. The four corrected passages are pinned by heading text, so the population cannot shrink to empty. Beside the render:
- A fence that shows a `description` must draw it.
- A static read: no fence may write `title` or `description` on a page whose effective `pageType` is `record`.
- Live control A: the Basic Usage fence without its `pageType` draws neither heading nor description.
- Live control B: the Detail fence with its heading moved back onto the page node draws no `h1`, while its buttons still draw.

The claim expected the pin in `packages/types` or `packages/layout`. It landed in `packages/components` because the assertion is a render. It needs React, a DOM project and `PageRenderer`, which lives in `@object-ui/components`. `@object-ui/types` is zero-dependency with no React, and its tests run in the node `unit` project. The sibling render pin for this guide's action passages, `guide-layout-page-buttons-7926.test.tsx`, sits in the same folder. The ledger row for the new reader is in `scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs`. An empty-frontmatter changeset declares that this releases nothing.

## Reverse verification

Each leg ran from committed head `f06910103`. Each restore was proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`. Mutations went through objectstack's `ablation-replace.mjs`, whose anchors had to hit. The predicted direction for every leg was red.

- (a) Delete Basic Usage's `"pageType": "app",` line (anchor 1 → 0): 4 failed / 9 passed. The failures are that fence's render, the description test, the static read and live control A.
- (b) Delete the Detail fence's `page:header` block: 2 failed / 10 passed (12). The failures are the population pin and live control B. The fence drops out of the render population, which is the case the population pin exists for.
- (c) Run against the whole guide at BASE `a1a44d621`: 8 failed / 5 passed. The failures are the four corrected passages' renders, the description test, the static read and both live controls.
- Ledger control: with the new row removed, `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit` exits 1 and names the pin (`unadjudicated-test`). My first attempt removed only the row's inner lines, which crashed the script instead of giving a verdict, so I redid it with the whole row.
- Anchor control: pointing the new `#page-header-pageheader` link at a wrong slug makes `scripts/check-doc-links.mjs` report a broken `[anchor]` link. Restored afterwards.

## Tests and gates (final head `01e353fa0`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run` over the new pin, every ledger reader of `layout.md` and `scripts/__tests__/markdown-test-inputs.test.ts`: Test Files 13 passed (13), Tests 173 passed (173). The new pin alone has 13 tests and runs in the `dom` project.
- The ledger script's other importers (8 files): Test Files 9 passed (9), Tests 324 passed (324).
- `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/components^...' --concurrency=2`: 7 successful. `pnpm --filter @object-ui/components type-check` exits 0, and the test program (`tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly`) includes the new pin.
- `pnpm check:doc-types`, `check:doc-fences`, `check:doc-example-ids`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:doc-example-readers` and `check:unreferenced-sources` all exit 0. `check:new-line-citations`: 0 new citations. `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`: links valid across 17 scan roots. `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit`: all adjudicated. `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-type-check-coverage` and `check-lint-coverage` all exit 0. `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the 4 paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- eslint `--no-inline-config --format json` over the 2 changed lintable files: 2 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. The narrowing is proven: `--print-config` gives 119 rules for the test file and 0 for `scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs`, which is outside the linted population. `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, and no custom rule reads the filesystem, so verdicts on untouched files cannot move.

NOT MEASURED:
- `pnpm check:doc-snippets` and `pnpm check:doc-examples`: exit 2, PRECONDITION NOT MET. The 34-package build closure does not fit the foreground cap, so this is a declared narrowing. These gates judge ts/tsx/typescript fences and JSDoc `@example` blocks. The diff adds or removes none of either, and the one `typescript` fence it edits (Schema API) is a declared `doc-snippet: fragment`. The unbuilt run's findings are 34 `unbuilt-package` and nothing about any document. CI runs both.
- The whole `packages/components` suite: exit 124 at 560 s with `--maxWorkers=2`, past the foreground cap, so this is also a declared narrowing. The diff adds one test file and changes no source in the package. Every reader of the edited guide ran above. CI runs the full suite.

## Acceptance notes

Found while measuring and not fixed here; reported to the seat:
- The same defect in another producer. All five schema-catalog documents under `examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/components-layout-page/` set `title` and `description` and no `pageType`. They are the live examples on the published `content/docs/components/layout/page.mdx`, one of them under "With Title and Description". Rendered through the real `SchemaRenderer`, each draws no `h1` and no description. With `pageType: "app"`, each draws both. That page's Schema block also omits `pageType`. Not fixed in place: it is another producer, and its catalog tests are a verification surface this card does not carry.
- `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md` (PageNodeSchema) teaches `"pageType": "detail"`, and its table lists `list`, `detail`, `form`, `dashboard`, `report` and `custom`. Both faces refuse `detail`, `custom` and `dashboard` with `invalid_value` at `pageType`. The declared set is record, home, app, utility and list, plus the visualization aliases.
- Observation, not filed: `title` and `description` on a record page pass both faces and draw nothing, and no diagnostic says so. The producers that taught the shape are this guide, now corrected, and the catalog above. A named diagnostic would be a new gate. Carrier: none.

Concurrency: draft PR objectui#11069 also edits `layout.md`, so whichever lands second merges `main`. `main` has moved since BASE, but none of the files this PR reads or edits changed.
